 COMMON - JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed petitions under Sec.166 of  Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-
 each in MVC.No.7386/2018 and MVC 7387/2018 and  Rs.15,00,000/- each in MVC No.7388/2018 and MVC  No.7404/2018 for the injuries sustained by them in road traffic  accident.
 2.

The brief case of the petitioners is that on 14.07.2018  at about 04.00 a.m., when petitioners were travelling as  occupants in Toyota Innova Car bearing Regn.No.KA-04-MH-1939  on Bengaluru-Tiruvannamalai Main Road, near Old Bus Depot,
 Pakkiripalayam, at that time driver of car drove the same at high  speed in a rash and negligent manner and lost control over the  vehicle and dashed against road side tree.

Due to which, they  were sustained grievous injuries and thereafter the petitioner in  MVC.No.7386/18 & MVC.No.7387/18 were shifted to Govt.
 Hospital, Thiruvannamalai and then shifted to Sriram Hospital,

The respondents being the insurer and  owner are jointly and severally liable to pay  SCCH-11 5 MVC 7386/2018 C/W 7387/2018,

Further contended that the 2 nd  respondent knowing fully well the driver was not having valid  and effective driving license authorizing him to driver class/type  of vehicle allegedly involved in the accident as on the date of  allege accident and he had entrusted his car to such a person to  drive at the time of accident.
Further contended that 1 st  respondent is not liable to pay any compensation or interest to  claimant in respect of above claim as Toyota car was not  involved in the accident and 2nd respondent has violated the  terms and conditions of policy and by entrusting consciously his  SCCH-11 6 MVC 7386/2018 C/W 7387/2018,

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The petitioner has not produced any medical bills.
The  petitioner has not produced any disability certificate and also  not examined the doctor to show that the petitioner has  sustained grievous injuries.
So, when the petitioner has not  produced any disability certificate or not examined doctor  regarding the injuries sustained by her in the accident, then she
is only entitled for global compensation.
By considering the facts  and circumstances of the case and also the injuries sustained by  the petitioner, the tribunal is of the view that the global  compensation of Rs.20,000/- is just and reasonable.
So, the  SCCH-11 13 MVC 7386/2018 C/W 7387/2018,
 7388/2018 & 7404/2018  petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of Rs.20,000/-
 with interest @ 6% from the date of petition till its realization.
The petitioner has not produced any disability  certificate and also not examined the doctor to show that she  has disabilities.
By considering the facts and  circumstances of the case and also the injuries sustained by the  petitioner, the tribunal is of the view that the global  compensation of Rs.30,000/- is just and reasonable.
In view of  holding issue No.1 in the affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for  SCCH-11 15 MVC 7386/2018 C/W 7387/2018,
 7388/2018 & 7404/2018  compensation.
To assess the compensation the tribunal has to  look in to several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained  by petitioners and amount spent by petitioner towards medical  expenses, food, extra nourishment and medical attendant,
 conveyance.
The petitioner has not produced disability certificate and also  not examined the doctor to show that she has disabilities.
So,
 when the petitioner has not produced any disability certificate or  not examined doctor regarding the injuries sustained by her in  the accident, then she is only entitled for global compensation.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also  the injuries sustained by the petitioner, the tribunal is of the  view that the global compensation of Rs.40,000/- is just and  reasonable.
So, the petitioner is entitled for Global  compensation of Rs.40,000/- with interest @ 6% from the date  of petition till its realization.
